122714.subject: Botany
122714.text: How does a leaf develop from the shoot apical meristem?
options: By developing at the node and bearing a bud in its axil
By developing at the stem and bearing a branch in its axil
By developing into a branch and bearing a node in its axil
By developing into a node and bearing a stem in its axil
122714.sol: The leaf is a lateral, generally flattened structure borne on the stem . It develops at the node and bears a bud in its axil. The axillary bud later develops into a branch. Leaves originate from shoot apical meristems and are arranged in an acropetal order. They are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis.

123185.subject: Botany
123185.sol: Microtubules are unbranched, hollow, submicroscopic tubules, which form the structural material of cilia, flagella, basal bodies, centrioles and spindle apparatus. Microtubules are built up of protofilaments formed of two related proteins, and -tubulins.

123273.subject: Botany
123273.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Epidermal hairs in stem are essential for plants to retain water Reason: The root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
123273.sol: On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular.The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

123282.subject: Botany
123282.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Mesophyll consists of two types of cells Reason:The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
123282.sol: Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma.

123531.subject: Botany
123531.text: What are the constituents of a cell that are synthesized during cell cycle?
options: DNA and other components of the cell
123531.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. 123640.subject: Botany
123640.text: Mitosis is important in the life of an organism because:
options: It produces both diploid daughter cells and multicellular organisms
123640.sol: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complement. The growth of multicellular organisms is due to mitosis. Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It therefore becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. A very significant contribution of mitosis is cell repair. The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are being constantly replace

124143.subject: Botany
124143.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer Reason: Movement of water by diffusion is called transpiration
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124143.sol: Polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer, they require a carrier protein of the membrane to facilitate their transport across the membrane.

124235.subject: Botany
124235.text: Centriole Structures Components A. Peripheral Fibrils 1. Central part of centriole B. Radial Spokes 2. Connects peripheral triplets C. Hub 3. Nine evenly spaced fibrils D. Triplets 4. Each peripheral fibril is a triplet

124645.subject: Botany
124645.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile Reason: The PGR abscisic acid belongs to this group of plant growth inhibitors

124645.sol: Charles Darwin and his son Francis Darwin when they observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source (phototropism). After a series of experiments, it was concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile .

124647.subject: Botany

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
124647.sol: During mid-1960s, three independent researches reported the purification and chemical characterisation of three different kinds of inhibitors: inhibitor-B, abscission II and dormin. Later all the three were proved to be chemically identical. It was named abscisic acid (ABA).

125064.sol: The complete combustion of glucose produces CO2 and H2O as end products. The combustion reaction requires Oxygen

125149.sol: The ratio of volume of CO2 evolved to the volume of oxygen consumed in respiration is called Respiratory quotient

transport oxygen for activity of nitrogenase

125973.sol: In most plants, by the time the fruit develops from the ovary, other floral parts degenerate and fall off. 126883.text: The major portion of the dry weight of plants comprises of:
126883.sol: The four most common elements in living organisms are H , C , O , N . These are also known as framework element. Carbon, hydrogen and oxygen together constitute about 94 % of the total dry weight of the plant.

127238.subject: Botany
127238.text: Where was the World Summit on Sustainable Development held in 2002?
127238.sol: Biodiversity knows no political boundaries and its conservation is therefore a collective responsibility of all nations. The historic Convention on Biological Diversity (‘The Earth Summit’) held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992, called upon all nations to take appropriate measures for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilisation of its benefits. 127424.sol: According to the data on biodiversity in the Amazonian rain forest, the number of species for the given groups are as follows: Invertebrates: more than 1,25,000 Plants: more than 40,000 Fishes: 3,000 Birds: 1,300 Mammals: 427 Arranging them in descending order of the number of species, we get: Invertebrates > Plants > Fishes > Birds > Mammals This corresponds to the sequence (d) > (a) > (c) > (b) > (e).

128978.sol: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) are primarily responsible for oxygen transport. Leukocytes (white blood cells) are involved in the defense against infections. Platelets are key players in blood clotting. Plasma carries nutrients and waste products.

To transport sodium ions into the axon.
To transport sodium ions outwards and potassium ions into the cell.
To transport both sodium and potassium ions into the cell.

129631.subject: Zoology
129631.text: Kidney Disorder Condition A. Glomerulonephritis 1. Formation of crystallised kidney stones of oxalates B. Glycosuria 2. Glucose in urine C. Renal Calculi 3. Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney D. Uremia 4. Accumulation of urea in blood
129631.sol: Glomerulonephritis is an inflammation of the glomeruli in the kidneys, which can impair kidney function. Glycosuria occurs when glucose is present in the urine, often associated with diabetes. Renal Calculi are crystallized kidney stones, typically composed of oxalates, that form in the kidneys. Uremia is the accumulation of urea and other waste products in the blood due to kidney failure.

131173.sol: Male reproductive system contains rete testis, vasa efferentia, Epididymis and vas deferens etc. Female reproductive system contain isthmus, ampulla, infundibulum and uterus etc.

132396.subject: Zoology
132396.text: Concept Example/Description A. Pleiotropy 1. A trait influenced by multiple genes, showing continuous variation B. Polygenic inheritance 2. A single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits C. Multiple alleles 3. Both alleles of a gene are equally expressed in the phenotype D. Codominance 4. More than two alternative forms of a gene (alleles) exist in the population
132396.sol: Pleiotropy: A single gene influences multiple phenotypic traits (e.g., Marfan syndrome). Polygenic inheritance: A trait influenced by multiple genes, showing continuous variation (e.g., skin color in humans). Multiple alleles: More than two alternative forms of a gene (alleles) exist in the population (e.g., ABO blood group). Codominance: Both alleles of a gene are equally expressed in the phenotype (e.g., AB blood type).

132816.subject: Zoology
132816.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Australian marsupials show convergent evolution. Reason: Marsupials in Australia evolved to fill similar ecological niches as placental mammals in other continents.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
132816.sol: Australian marsupials are an example of adaptive radiation, but also mentions that "placental mammals in Australia have evolved to resemble marsupials," illustrating convergent evolution.

132938.subject: Zoology
132938.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The Cenozoic era is considered the 'Age of Mammals' as they flourished and dominated the earth during this time. options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Following the extinction of dinosaurs at the end of the Mesozoic era, mammals underwent adaptive radiation and became the dominant land animals during the Cenozoic era, which is why it is called the 'Age of Mammals'. Reason (R) is false. Mammals did not originate in the Cenozoic era. No negative impacts on the environment

95786.sol: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium, or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast (Saccharomyces). 95870.text: Which of the following feature is common to bacteria, mosses and fungus?

96464.sol: Bacteria are essential decomposers in nature. 97110.subject: Botany
97110.text: Flowers of Pea possess the same symmetry as that of
97110.sol: When a flower can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, Gulmohar, bean, cassia. When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the center, it is said to be actinomorphic, e.g., mustard, datura, chili. A flower is asymmetric (irregular) if it cannot be divided into two similar halves by any vertical plane passing through the center, as in canna.

97425.text: Conifers differ from grasses in the
97425.sol: Conifers (gymnosperms) differ from grasses (angiosperms) because in gymnosperms, the female gametophyte is actually endosperm which is made before fertilisation. However, in grasses, endosperm is a tissue formed by the fertilization of second male gamete to polar nuclei. Moreover, in gymnosperms, the endosperm is a haploid tissue, whereas in angiosperms it is triploid.

In conifers, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area
97552.sol: In Gymnosperms, leaves are either simple or compound. In some gymnosperms like Cycas, the pinnate leaves persist for a few years. Leaves of gymnosperms are well-adapted for adverse conditions like to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity, and wind, etc. In conifers, like Pinus, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area. Their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss.

97894.subject: Botany
97894.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes have self-consciousness.
The sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in our body is metabolism.
Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free system.
97894.sol: Consciousness is a defining property because it is seen in all living organisms from prokaryotes to complex eukaryotes without any exception but self-consciousness is a characteristic feature of human only because a human is the only organism which is aware of himself. All reactions taking place inside the body are collectively called metabolism which is also a defining property of living beings.

306438.subject: Physics
306438.text: A voltmeter's net resistance should be large in order to ensure that
options: it does not appreciably alter the potential difference being measured
it can measure high potential differences
306438.sol: A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the component whose potential difference is to be measured. If the resistance of the voltmeter is not large, it will draw a significant amount of current from the main circuit. This reduces the current flowing through the component, thereby altering the potential difference across it. To ensure that the voltmeter does not appreciably alter the potential difference being measured, its net resistance must be very large (ideally infinite).

306627.text: With an increase in the mass number A , the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus
options: varies in a manner dependent on the specific value of A
306627.sol: The binding energy per nucleon curve shows that for low mass numbers, the binding energy per nucleon generally increases with an increase in mass number A . It reaches a maximum value of about 8.8 MeV for A 56 (Iron). For mass numbers greater than 56 , the binding energy per nucleon gradually decreases, reaching about 7.6 MeV for Uranium. Therefore, the binding energy per nucleon does not monotonically increase or decrease, but varies in a manner dependent on the specific value of the mass number A .
